blocks.text: Upper Respiratory-tract Infections (URIs) affect the nose, throat, sinuses, and larynx and can be easily transmitted from person to person through respiratory droplets.

It is the inflammation of the lining of the sinuses (four paired air-filled spaces that surround the nasal cavity i.e., under the eyes; above the eyes; between the eyes and behind the eyes). It may be acute (lasts for 7 to 10 days) or chronic (lasts longer than 12 week). Most case of sinusitis are due to viral infections; some may be due to bacterial infections and rare cases may also involve fungal infections.

blocks.alt: A head in side view facing right, with four coloured sinus groups around the nose and eyes: one above the eyes in the forehead, one behind the eyes, one between the eyes and nose, and one under the eyes in the cheek.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.10: Sinuses (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 10.10).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Above eyes, Behind eyes, Between eyes and nose, Under eyes.

blocks.text: Symptoms of sinusitis include fever, plugged nose, pus-like nasal discharge, loss of sense of smell, facial pain, a feeling that phlegm is falling from the back of nose into throat, and headache that is sometimes aggravated by bending over.

Treatment: Most cases are caused by viruses and resolve without antibiotics. If it is due to a bacterial infection, antibiotics or sulpha drugs are usually prescribed. Beside it, the physician may also prescribe nebulization which can be useful in reducing inflammation in the sinuses and nose and to accelerate recovery. For chronic or recurring sinusitis, treatment may include nasal surgery in which the pathogens and mucous are removed.

It is the inflammation of the middle ear. Otitis may be acute (rapid onset) or chronic (lasts more than six weeks). The common cause of otitis media accumulation of fluid in Eustachian tube, which cannot be drained from the middle ear. When this fluid is not drained, it allows the growth of bacteria and viruses in the middle ear that lead to otitis media.

blocks.alt: A section through the ear: the external ear and ear canal end at the eardrum; behind it the middle ear with its three small bones is inflamed and partly filled with fluid; beyond it lie the inner ear with its semicircular canals, cochlea and nerve. The Eustachian tube runs down from the middle ear and is narrowed.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.11: Otitis media (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 10.11).
blocks.long_description: Labels: External ear, Middle ear, Internal ear, Inflammation and fluid accumulation in the middle ear, Eustachian tube (narrowed).

blocks.text: Symptoms of otitis media include severe ear pain, pulling at one or both ears, fever, fluid draining from ear(s), loss of balance, and hearing difficulties.
Treatments include oral and topical pain killers and antibiotics (if caused by bacterial infection).
